The White House said Aaron Lukas, then a deputy director, would serve as acting director. title: USDA says it will not use emergency funds for November SNAP benefits
description_medium: During the federal shutdown, the Agriculture Department said it would not use emergency funds to issue November SNAP benefits. A Reuters report on the department’s October 24 memo said more than 41 million people could lose food assistance at month’s end; USDA said the contingency money was not legally available for that purpose.
description_long: During the 2025 federal government shutdown, the U.S. Department of Agriculture said it would not use emergency funds to issue November Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits. Reuters reported that an October 24 USDA memo said more than 41 million people were at risk of losing benefits when the month ended. The department said the $5 billion contingency fund was reserved for disasters and was not legally available to pay SNAP benefits. USDA also said it would not use other funds or reimburse states that chose to cover benefits themselves. The decision left states, food-aid organizations and households facing uncertainty as the shutdown continued.
